region: Union Springs · Cayuga Lake, Finger Lakes, New York
about: Mo Chuisle is the flagship of Heart & Hands, the Cayuga Lake winery of Tom and Susan Higgins. The name is Irish Gaelic, roughly “my pulse” or “my heartbeat,” used to mean “my darling,” and it fits a winery named for the Claddagh ring. The Higginses bought their slope above the lake’s eastern shore near Union Springs in 2007, after Tom had spent years hunting for limestone on geological maps, and planted Pinot Noir there in 2010. Mo Chuisle is their estate reserve, first made from the 2012 harvest.

It comes from the estate vineyard, which lies on Onondaga limestone about 650 feet from the shore at Carr’s Cove and is farmed without herbicides or insecticides. The grapes are hand-picked in the early morning, sorted berry by berry, and fermented in small open-top vats with hand punch-downs twice a day. The wine is moved by gravity into François Frères French oak barrels, with Tom choosing the forest, toast and share of new wood for each lot.

Mo Chuisle has drawn some of the strongest reviews of any Finger Lakes Pinot Noir: James Suckling’s Stuart Pigott gave the 2020 96 points and the 2022 98. For this 2021, from a wet late summer rescued by a dry September, the winery notes black cherry, chalky minerality, cranberry and cassis, with a long, dry finish.
